Last updated November 14, 2026.

Scottsdale at a glance

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 243,006 (Census Bureau).
Selling in Scottsdale?

What are your options for selling a house fast in Scottsdale, AZ?

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as-is. In Scottsdale the right choice depends on how much the house needs, because the median owner-occupied home value is $789,800 and a repair bill on a home that size can be large.

A listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers and the highest price for a house in good shape. A cash sale trades some of that price for speed and certainty, and it suits owners facing a relocation, an inherited property, a tenant problem or a stalled renovation. Ask each buyer for the net figure after repairs, fees and carrying costs, then compare the totals.

How is Scottsdale laid out, and why does it matter for a sale?

Scottsdale is long and narrow: about 31 miles from north to south across 184.5 square miles, with Phoenix on the west, Tonto National Forest to the north, the McDowell Mountains on the east and the Salt River to the south. It was named in 1894 for Winfield Scott, an Army chaplain, and incorporated in 1951 with about 2,000 residents. The Census Bureau now estimates 243,006 residents as of July 1, 2025.

The city is commonly split into four areas, and buyers shop them differently:

  • South Scottsdale, from McKellips Road north to Thomas Road, includes the SkySong research center tied to Arizona State University
  • Old Town, the downtown core of galleries, restaurants and older streets
  • Central Scottsdale, also called the Shea Corridor, from Camelback Road north to Shea Boulevard
  • North Scottsdale, the northern end of the city

Say which area your house is in when you ask for offers. Comparable sales a mile apart can be far apart in price.

What does Census data say about Scottsdale housing?

Scottsdale is an older, higher-income city with small households and a large share of retirees. The figures below are Census Bureau numbers for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

MeasureScottsdale
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate243,006
Households118,637
Persons per household2.03
Owner-occupied housing rate67.0%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$789,800
Median gross rent$2,013
Median household income$110,886
Residents age 65 and over26.4%

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Scottsdale city, Arizona.

With 67 percent of homes owner-occupied, about one in three households rents, so rentals are a real part of the market and some buyers will want to know what a house can earn.

Which employers, schools and roads shape Scottsdale buyer demand?

Health care, finance, defense and tourism anchor the local economy. The city's 2022 financial report listed HonorHealth (7,131 employees), Vanguard (2,770), General Dynamics Mission Systems (2,700), the City of Scottsdale (2,612), the Scottsdale Unified School District (2,093) and the Mayo Clinic (1,917) as its top employers. The Scottsdale Airpark around the municipal airport is a major employment center, and winter visitors from colder states often end up buying second homes here. The Census Bureau counted $3,062,966,000 in accommodation and food services sales in 2022, which shows how much the visitor economy matters, and the mean commute for workers is 21.6 minutes.

Public schools are split among several districts, which is worth stating in any listing:

  • Scottsdale Unified serves most of the city and runs five high schools: Arcadia, Coronado, Chaparral, Desert Mountain and Saguaro
  • Paradise Valley Unified serves North Scottsdale, including Horizon and Pinnacle high schools
  • Cave Creek Unified, Fountain Hills Unified, Balsz Elementary and Phoenix Union High School districts cover other pieces

Loop 101 is the main freeway, Valley Metro runs the regional buses, and the city operates a free Downtown Trolley and Neighborhood Trolley. Climate is dry desert, with a mean July high near 104 degrees and about 8.7 inches of rain a year.

Can a buyer rent your Scottsdale house short term?

Yes, but Scottsdale requires a city license for any rental under 30 days. A buyer who plans nightly or weekly stays should know the steps before bidding, and a seller can use them as a selling point. The annual license costs $250 per property, and rentals of 30 days or longer do not need it.

The city lists these steps for an operator:

  • Get a Transaction Privilege Tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue for each rental, listing Scottsdale (SC) as a region code
  • Apply for the Scottsdale license under Ordinance 4566
  • Within 30 days of receiving it, notify the neighbors beside and across the street, and carry at least $500,000 in liability coverage
  • Register the property with the Maricopa County Assessor before anyone occupies it
  • Post the required notice inside the front door and the backyard door

Properties with a pool, hot tub or spa also face pool barrier rules. State law (A.R.S. 9-500.39) limits what a city can require, and it caps a permit fee at the actual cost or $250, whichever is less. Ask the City of Scottsdale licensing office whether a license already exists for your address.

How do you record a Scottsdale sale in Maricopa County?

The deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder, and it needs a completed affidavit of property value unless an exemption is noted on it (A.R.S. 11-1133). The affidavit gives the price, financing, parcel number, sale date and whether the home will be owner-occupied or rented. A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts, among other transfers, a deed of gift and a transfer with only nominal consideration between parent and child, spouses or siblings.

The Recorder lists a $30 fee for most documents, $1 per page for copies and $3 for a certification. Your title or escrow company normally handles the filing and tells you the exact amount on the closing statement.

When is Maricopa County property tax due for a Scottsdale owner?

Tax bills are due in two halves, October 1 and March 1, and become delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1 (A.R.S. 42-18052). The Maricopa County Treasurer's 2026 calendar shows first-half taxes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026, so that date has passed. Final delinquent notices for unpaid 2025 taxes go out December 1, and December 31 is the last day to pay 2026 full-year taxes of more than $100 without interest.

Ask the Maricopa County Treasurer for a current balance on your parcel before you list, and have your title company explain how the current year is divided at closing.

More questions about Scottsdale, AZ

How fast can a Scottsdale house sell for cash?

A cash sale can close faster than a financed one, because there is no lender appraisal or loan approval. The actual date depends on the title search, any liens or probate steps, and when both sides sign. Ask the buyer to give you a written closing date.

Do I need a Scottsdale license to sell a house that was a short-term rental?

The license covers operating a rental of under 30 days, so ask the City of Scottsdale licensing office what happens to yours when the property sells. A new owner who continues short-term renting should expect to apply for their own.

What does it cost to record a deed in Maricopa County?

The Maricopa County Recorder lists $30 for most documents. Copies are $1 per page and a certification is $3. Arizona sets the same $30 fee by statute in A.R.S. 11-475.

Which school district is my Scottsdale home in?

It depends on the street. Scottsdale Unified serves most of the city, Paradise Valley Unified serves North Scottsdale, and parts belong to Cave Creek, Fountain Hills, Balsz and Phoenix Union districts. Check your address with the district before you advertise a school.

Are Scottsdale property taxes still open for 2026?

The first half of 2026 became delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, 2026. Maricopa County lists December 31 as the last day to pay full-year 2026 taxes without interest, and the second half is due March 1, 2027. Contact the County Treasurer for your balance.

How can you sell a house fast in Surprise, AZ?

You can list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. In Surprise, a house in good shape tends to suit a listing, and a house that needs work or has a deadline attached tends to suit a direct sale.

Surprise is a city in Maricopa County. The Census Bureau estimates 175,304 residents as of July 1, 2025, and 79.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median value for an owner-occupied home is $435,100. When you gather offers, ask each buyer to state the closing date, who pays recording and title charges, and whether repairs are priced in.

How did Surprise grow into a city of 175,000?

Surprise grew from a farm settlement into one of the larger cities in the state within about a generation. It was founded in 1938 by Flora Mae Statler, incorporated as a town on December 12, 1960, and first built as inexpensive housing for agricultural workers. The original townsite is bounded by Greenway Road on the south, El Mirage Road on the east, Bell Road on the north and Dysart Road on the west. City Hall now stands on the site of a former auxiliary airfield for Luke Air Force Base, and the old runway outlines still show in aerial photos.

YearPopulation
2000 census30,848
2010 census117,517
2020 census143,148
July 1, 2025 estimate175,304

Source: U.S. Census Bureau decennial counts and QuickFacts.

How the town got its name is still debated. Some records say Statler chose it because she would be surprised if the town ever amounted to much, while others point to Surprise, Nebraska, the hometown of her husband Homer Ludden. Local government is a mayor elected at large and a six-member council elected by district, in staggered four-year terms. The city library system, created in 2023 when Surprise took over three county libraries, includes the Surprise Regional Library on the Recreation Campus and branches in the original townsite and in north Surprise.

The city covers 110.5 square miles at 1,385 feet of elevation. Population is up 22.5 percent from the April 2020 estimates base, so much of the housing is recent construction, and a buyer will compare yours with newer homes.

What do the Census numbers show for Surprise housing?

Surprise skews toward owners, families and retirees at once. The Census Bureau reports these figures for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

  • Households: 56,506, averaging 2.71 persons
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $435,100
  • Median gross rent: $2,033
  • Median household income: $96,711
  • Residents under 18: 23.1 percent; age 65 and over: 22.2 percent
  • Mean commute to work: 30.2 minutes

The long commute matters when you describe the house. Many residents work elsewhere in the Valley, so the distance to Loop 303, U.S. 60 and the Valley Metro express route to Glendale belongs in your listing.

A large age-restricted community also sits inside the city. Sun City Grand, for residents 45 and older, was founded in 1996, finished building homes in 2005 and has four golf courses. If your house is inside it, ask the community for its resale rules before you accept an offer.

Which schools, jobs and roads draw buyers to Surprise?

The Dysart Unified School District serves most of the city, and the Nadaburg Unified School District serves a small section in the north. Confirm which one applies to your address before you advertise a school. Ottawa University opened a campus in Surprise in 2017.

The largest employers in the 2023 Council of Governments database were:

  • Dysart Unified School District, 1,760 employees
  • City of Surprise, 1,170
  • Walmart, 890
  • Sun Health Foundation, 570
  • Fry's Food and Drug, 550

A foreign trade zone at the southeast corner of the city, the Southwest Railplex industrial district, has rail access through BNSF. Roads are Loop 303 and U.S. 60. Valley Metro runs express route 571 between Surprise and Glendale, and the WeRIDE on-demand service had been scheduled to end on July 1, 2025.

Which Surprise city offices matter when you sell or rent a house?

Planning, permits and building safety all sit in the city's Community Development Department. Its Permits and Applications page covers everything from a commercial project to a resident adding a patio, and Building Inspections and Plan Review covers construction inspections. If you have an open permit or finished work without one, ask Community Development to clarify before you list.

The city also runs a Rental Accountability Ordinance, which sits under Code Enforcement along with a page on sober living homes. If the house is currently rented, ask Surprise Code Enforcement what that ordinance requires of you and what a buyer inherits. Arizona law (A.R.S. 9-500.39) separately restricts what cities may require of short-term rentals, allowing a permit with a fee of no more than $250 or the cost of issuing it, an emergency contact and proof of $500,000 in liability insurance.

How is a Surprise sale recorded in Maricopa County?

A deed is recorded with the Maricopa County Recorder. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires a completed affidavit of property value with the deed, signed by buyer and seller or their agents, and the recorder must refuse the deed without it unless an exemption is noted. A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts transfers such as a deed of gift, a nominal-consideration transfer between family members, and a conveyance made under a court order.

Maricopa County charges $30 to record most documents, $1 per page for copies and $3 for a certification. Title or escrow companies normally file for you, and your closing statement will show the exact charges.

When are property taxes due for a Surprise homeowner?

Maricopa County collects in two halves due October 1 and March 1, with delinquency after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1, moved to the next business day when those fall on a weekend (A.R.S. 42-18052). For 2026 the Treasurer's calendar shows the first half delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 2, a date already behind us. It also shows December 1 for final delinquent notices on unpaid 2025 taxes and December 31 as the last day to pay 2026 full-year taxes over $100 without interest. A full-year bill of $100 or less is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on December 31.

Ask the Maricopa County Treasurer for the balance on your parcel before signing, and have the title company explain how the current year is divided between you and the buyer.

More questions about Surprise, AZ

Is Surprise a good place to sell a house quickly?

Speed depends on condition, price and how you sell. The city has grown 22.5 percent since the April 2020 estimates base, so there are many nearby comparable sales to price against. Compare the net amount from a listing, a private sale and a cash offer.

Which county records a Surprise home sale?

Maricopa County. The Maricopa County Recorder records the deed, and the fee for most documents is $30. The deed needs an affidavit of property value or a written exemption under Arizona law.

Do I need a permit to sell a house with unpermitted work in Surprise?

Ask the Surprise Community Development Department how the city handles work done without a permit. Unpermitted work can come up in a buyer's inspection or a lender's review, so tell the buyer what you know.

Which school district serves my Surprise address?

Most of the city is in the Dysart Unified School District, and a small northern section is in the Nadaburg Unified School District. Confirm your address with the district before you list.

Can I sell a rented house in Surprise with tenants in it?

Check your lease and your notice duties first, and ask Surprise Code Enforcement about the Rental Accountability Ordinance. A buyer who wants the tenants kept should say so in writing before you accept an offer.

How do you sell a house fast in Sierra Vista, AZ?

You choose between listing the house, selling it yourself and taking a cash offer, and the best route depends on how soon you need to close and how much work the house needs. Sierra Vista has one feature that sets its market apart from other Arizona cities: Fort Huachuca, the Army post at the northwest edge of town, which drives a steady cycle of arrivals and departures.

The Census Bureau counts 7,133 veterans in the city and estimates 44,907 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is 0.9 percent below the April 2020 estimates base of 45,310, so the population is flat rather than growing, which is worth keeping in mind when you set a price. If a permanent change of station, a deployment or a family move sets your deadline, ask each buyer for a written closing date as well as a price.

Where is Sierra Vista and what is it like?

Sierra Vista is the commercial center of Cochise County, in the southwest corner of the county about 75 miles southeast of Tucson. Tombstone is 15 miles northeast and Bisbee 20 miles southeast, and the Mexican border is about 15 miles south. The city covers 152.5 square miles at 4,623 feet of elevation, with the Huachuca Mountains on the southwest side and the San Pedro River just east of the city limits. State Routes 90 and 92 are the main roads.

The area grew around Camp Huachuca, founded in 1877, and the post was annexed into the city in 1971. Nearly half of local jobs are government jobs, the professional and technical services sector is large because of Army contracts, and Wick Communications, a newspaper publisher, is headquartered here. The Mall at Sierra Vista and several big-box retailers make the city the shopping hub for the county.

At that elevation the weather is milder than the Phoenix area. Winter lows average 20 to 30 degrees, frost can last into mid or late April, and the July and August monsoon delivers almost half of the year's rain. The record low is 4 degrees and the record high is 110. Heating, windows and roof drainage are sensible things to have answers about before a buyer asks.

What do Census numbers say about Sierra Vista homes?

Home values here sit well below the Phoenix-area cities, and rent is higher than in border towns such as San Luis. The Census Bureau reports these figures for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 62.0 percent
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $254,200
  • Median gross rent: $1,150
  • Households: 18,862, with 2.29 persons per household
  • Median household income: $70,291
  • Residents age 65 and over: 21.8 percent
  • Mean commute: 17.5 minutes

A 62 percent ownership rate means nearly four in ten households rent, so rentals are a real share of the market. Public schools come from the Sierra Vista Unified School District, which runs Buena High School, one middle school and six elementary schools. Higher education is available at Cochise College and the University of Arizona College of Applied Science and Technology.

What Sierra Vista city rules apply to a sale or a rental?

Repairs go through Community Development, which you can reach at (520) 417-4413 if you are unsure whether a project needs a permit. The city asks for plans as one complete, editable PDF with no passwords. Work in the public right-of-way and pool or spa drain applications go to the Public Works Department, and home-based business permits run through the City Clerk.

Landlords should know how the city treats rental income. The city's published property tax rate is $0.1056 per $100 of assessed value and its sales tax rate is 1.95 percent. A property owner who uses a management company can operate under that company's city business license. An owner who manages the property and must collect and remit real property rental tax needs a city business license of their own. The city is a program city, so the Arizona Department of Revenue collects the privilege taxes, and the city cannot give binding tax opinions.

Arizona law also limits what a city can require of short-term rentals (A.R.S. 9-500.39), including a permit fee capped at $250 or the actual cost and proof of $500,000 in liability coverage. Ask the City Clerk whether your buyer needs a permit for nightly rentals.

How do you record a Sierra Vista sale in Cochise County?

The deed is recorded with the Cochise County Recorder. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires a completed affidavit of property value with each deed, and the recorder must refuse a deed that lacks one unless it notes an exemption under A.R.S. 11-1134. Exemptions include:

  • A deed of gift
  • A conveyance made under a court order
  • A transfer for only nominal consideration between parent and child, spouses, or siblings

The standard recording fee under A.R.S. 11-475 is $30 per instrument. Ask the Recorder for the current mail-in and electronic filing steps, and let your title company confirm the total on the closing statement.

After the deed is recorded, the Cochise County Assessor changes the owner's name on the tax roll. If the old owner receives a tax notice after the sale, the Treasurer asks that it be returned to P.O. Box 1778, Bisbee, AZ 85603 with a note that the property sold.

When are Cochise County property taxes due for a Sierra Vista home?

Cochise County bills in two installments, and a combined bill covers the city, county, schools, college and special districts. Tax notices are mailed in September, and the county asks you to call if yours has not arrived by October 10. Taxes are due whether or not a notice arrives.

InstallmentDueDelinquent after 5:00 p.m.
First halfOctober 1November 1
Second halfMarch 1May 1
Total bill of $100 or lessOctober 1, in fullDecember 31

Source: Cochise County Treasurer FAQ and A.R.S. 42-18052. A weekend or holiday date moves to the next business day, so November 1, 2026 became Monday, November 2, and the first-half date has now passed.

After a delinquency date, simple interest runs at 16 percent a year, charged as 1.333 percent a month. Taxes still unpaid after May 1 and into the following January take a further 5 percent penalty, and the county sells its lien on delinquent parcels each February. The Treasurer notes that the tax lien attaches to the property each January no matter who owns it, so ask for a current balance before you sign a contract. If you think your value is wrong, an appeal concerns the property's value, and it starts when the notice of value arrives. Contact the Cochise County Assessor for that process.

More questions about Sierra Vista, AZ

Does Fort Huachuca affect how fast a Sierra Vista house sells?

It affects who is looking. The post is the city's main employer and nearly half of local jobs are in government. Set your price and closing date with that in mind, and ask each buyer for a written closing date.

Do I need a city business license to rent my Sierra Vista house?

It depends on how you manage it. If a property management company handles the rental, you can operate under its city business license. If you manage it yourself and must collect and remit real property rental tax, you need your own city license. Call Community Development or the City Clerk to confirm.

What does it cost to record a deed in Cochise County?

Arizona sets the fee at $30 per instrument under A.R.S. 11-475, with copies at $1 per page and $3 for a certificate. Ask the Cochise County Recorder or your title company for current steps and any extra charges.

What happens if my Cochise County taxes are delinquent when I sell?

The delinquent amount carries interest at 16 percent a year and may be sold as a lien in February. Because the lien attaches to the property each January, ask the Cochise County Treasurer for a payoff figure and have your title company handle payment at closing.

Can I sell a Sierra Vista house without repairs?

Yes. Arizona does not require repairs before a sale, so you can sell as-is. A financed buyer may ask for repairs after an inspection, while a cash buyer builds them into the offer. Work done without a permit is worth raising with Community Development at (520) 417-4413 before you list.

How can you sell a house fast in San Luis, AZ?

You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the property as-is. A San Luis sale moves fastest when the paperwork is ready before the buyer is, so gather your deed, any loan payoff figure and your latest Yuma County tax bill first.

San Luis sits in the southwest corner of Arizona, right against the border crossing with San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora. That location drives demand for houses near the crossing and the highways to Yuma. The Census Bureau estimates 42,030 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 18.5 percent from the April 2020 estimates base of 35,464.

A cash buyer can skip showings, repairs and lender appraisals. The trade is a price below what a fully repaired listing might reach, so compare the net figure from each route, not only the headline number.

What kind of city is San Luis for a home seller?

San Luis is a young, border-edge city in Yuma County that grew very quickly in the last four decades. It was established in 1930 with the opening of a border-crossing station, incorporated in 1979, and went from 1,946 residents in 1980 to 35,257 in the 2020 census. Between 2006 and 2012 the city annexed more than 16,000 acres, much of it on the eastern side where a newer commercial port of entry is planned.

The town is low and flat. Its elevation is 167 feet, and the lowest point in Arizona, about 70 feet, is on the Colorado River where it leaves the state at San Luis. Summers are severe: the mean daily high is 106 degrees in July and the record is 124. Rain is scarce at about 3.7 inches a year, so buyers and inspectors tend to ask about the age and condition of the cooling system and the roof.

Local jobs come from retail, agriculture, manufacturing and light industry on both sides of the border. The city's 2014 financial report listed the Gadsden Elementary School District, ACT Advanced Call Center Technologies and the Arizona State Prison Complex in Yuma as its largest employers, each with roughly 800 or more staff. Highway access is through U.S. 95 and State Route 195 to Yuma, and Yuma County Area Transit connects to Greyhound in Yuma.

What do San Luis housing numbers look like?

Housing costs are modest and households are large. The Census Bureau figures below are for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

MeasureSan Luis
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate42,030
Households9,562
Persons per household3.41
Owner-occupied housing rate68.4%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$224,900
Median gross rent$741
Median household income$59,400
Mean commute to work26.9 minutes

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, San Luis city, Arizona.

Two details matter for a seller. First, about 91 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, so a listing, a disclosure packet or a contract explained in Spanish reaches more buyers. Second, the gap between a median home value of $224,900 and median rent of $741 is worth knowing when you set a price.

Which schools and neighborhoods will buyers ask about?

Most San Luis addresses feed the Gadsden Elementary School District, which runs Arizona Desert, Cesar Chavez, Desert View, Ed Pastor, Gadsden and Rio Colorado elementary schools plus San Luis Middle School and Southwest Junior High School. Sun Valley Elementary belongs to the Somerton Elementary School District, and San Luis High School is part of the Yuma Union High School District.

Buyers also look at:

  • Distance to the San Luis I port of entry for anyone who crosses regularly
  • The drive to Yuma on U.S. 95 or State Route 195
  • Whether the lot is in the newer eastern annexation area
  • Garage, shade and cooling equipment, given the heat

Ask your agent or buyer which school boundary applies to your street, since boundaries come from the school districts.

What city rules affect selling or fixing up a house in San Luis?

Repairs and additions go through the Building Safety Division, and land-use questions go to Planning and Zoning. Building Safety takes the permit application, a full set of plans or drawings that show the scope of work, and a site plan. Electronic PDF files are preferred, and hard copies run to two sets for residential work. The division can be reached at 928-341-8565. Planning and Zoning, at 1090 E. Union Street, handles land use applications, variances and temporary use permits and can be reached at 928-341-8563.

If you did work on the house without a permit, ask Building Safety what it needs before you list. A buyer's lender or inspector may raise it later.

Short-term renting is governed by state law. A.R.S. 9-500.39 bars a city from prohibiting short-term rentals but lets it require a permit with a fee of no more than $250 or the actual cost of issuing it, proof of $500,000 in liability coverage and an emergency contact. Ask the City of San Luis whether it runs such a permit if your buyer plans nightly rentals.

How is a San Luis sale transferred and recorded?

The deed is recorded with the Yuma County Recorder, and the recorder must refuse a deed that lacks a completed affidavit of property value unless it carries an exemption note (A.R.S. 11-1133). The affidavit is signed by seller and buyer or their agents and lists the sale price, financing type, parcel number and whether the home will be owner-occupied or rented.

Some transfers need no affidavit. Under A.R.S. 11-1134 the list includes:

  • A deed of gift
  • A transfer for only nominal consideration between parent and child, spouses, grandparent and grandchild, or siblings
  • A conveyance made under a court order
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already recorded

The exemption has to be written on the face of the deed. The standard recording fee set by A.R.S. 11-475 is $30 per instrument, with copies at $1 a page and $3 for a certificate. Ask the Yuma County Recorder for current e-recording and mail-in instructions, and ask your title company to confirm the figure before closing.

When are property taxes due on a San Luis home?

Yuma County bills property tax in two halves. The first half is due October 1 and the second half March 1, and state law makes each half delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and May 1 (A.R.S. 42-18052). If a delinquency date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day, which is why the county calendar shows November 2, 2026 for the first half of 2026.

That date has now passed. Yuma County lists December 31 as the last day to pay 2026 taxes in full without interest, and the second half of 2026 is due March 1, 2027 and delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 3, 2027. Delinquent 2025 taxes pick up a 5 percent penalty on January 1, 2027 and go to the county tax lien sale on February 18, 2027.

Ask the Yuma County Treasurer for the current balance on your parcel before you sign a contract, and ask the title company how the current year will be split between you and the buyer.

More questions about San Luis, AZ

Do I need to make repairs before selling a house in San Luis?

No law requires repairs before a sale, so you can sell as-is. What changes is who buys. A buyer using a lender will usually ask for repairs after an inspection, while a cash buyer prices the repairs into the offer. If you did any past work without a permit, call the San Luis Building Safety Division at 928-341-8565 first.

Who records the deed when a San Luis house sells?

The Yuma County Recorder does. The deed must come with a completed affidavit of property value or a written exemption, and the standard fee under A.R.S. 11-475 is $30 per instrument. A title or escrow company normally handles the filing.

Is there a transfer tax when selling in San Luis?

Arizona law requires an affidavit of property value and a recording fee when a deed is recorded. Ask your title company for the full closing statement so you can see every charge before you sign.

What happens if I fall behind on Yuma County property taxes?

Taxes unpaid after the delinquency date are penalized and, in time, sold as a lien. For 2025 taxes, Yuma County lists a 5 percent penalty on January 1, 2027 and a tax lien sale on February 18, 2027. Contact the Yuma County Treasurer for a payoff figure.

Can the buyer of my San Luis house use it as a short-term rental?

Often yes, because A.R.S. 9-500.39 stops Arizona cities from banning short-term rentals. A city may still require a permit, insurance of at least $500,000 and an emergency contact. The buyer should ask the City of San Luis what applies.
